children: Zumiez reported second-quarter fiscal 2026 net sales of $209.0 million, a 2.5% decline versus the prior-year quarter, and a net loss of $2.7 million, or $0.17 per share. For the six months ended August 1, 2026, net sales rose 0.9% to $402.3 million while year-to-date net loss was $16.0 million, or $1.00 per share. The company introduced third-quarter guidance of $222–$226 million in net sales and EPS of $0.00–$0.10 and disclosed continued store optimization and share repurchases impacting cash.
Quarterly net sales: $208.964 million for the three months ended August 1, 2026 (down 2.5% from $214.275 million).
Quarterly gross profit: $73.851 million, representing 35.3% of sales (compared with $76.018 million and 35.5% a year earlier).
Operating (loss) (profit) for the quarter: $(1.324) million, or -0.6% of sales (prior year operating profit of $0.107 million, 0.1% of sales).
Quarterly net loss: $(2.743) million, or $(0.17) basic and diluted loss per share (prior year net loss $(1.002) million, or $(0.06) per share).
Six months net sales: $402.313 million (up 0.9% from $398.618 million); six months net loss: $(16.009) million, or $(1.00) per share.
Regional performance: U.S. business weakened—primarily due to softness in footwear and lower traffic—while international regions continued to grow, partially offsetting U.S. declines.
Store footprint changes: Company plans to open approximately 5 new North America stores and close roughly 16 stores in fiscal 2026 (10 in North America, 6 internationally).

Share repurchases: Repurchased 1.2 million shares in Q2 at an average cost of $19.30 per share (Q2 total ~$23.2 million); fiscal year-to-date repurchases of 1.5 million shares for ~$29.5 million at an average cost of $20.07 per share.

Liquidity and cash use: Cash and marketable securities totaled $97.3 million at August 1, 2026, down from $106.7 million a year earlier, driven by share repurchases and capital expenditures partially offset by operating cash flow.
Merchandise and customer focus: Company emphasized refining merchandise assortments and enhancing customer experience initiatives ahead of the holiday season to improve trajectory.
